plan.title: My own project plan
plan.help: Plan a project of your own on one page. It saves on this device as you type.
plan.template:
Project name: [short name]

One sentence: This program takes [input] and gives [output] for [who].

The problem it solves: [why someone would want it]

Input: [what goes in: a file, a list, text]
Output: [what comes out: a file, a report, a message]

Steps:
1. [small step]
2. [small step]
3. [small step]

Done when: [3 things you can check, for example "it cleans the sample file", "it never crashes on bad lines", "the README explains how to run it"]

Not now: [ideas for later, so you do not add them today]

projects.title: Customer list cleaner
projects.summary: Clean a messy customer list with fake data and write a short report. This is your first portfolio project.

steps.title: Plan it on one page
steps.text: Say what goes in, what comes out, and when it is done.

steps.title: Make a messy fake customers.csv
steps.text: The project lesson makes the file for you. Never use real customer data.

steps.title: Clean the emails
steps.text: Exercise 1: clean_email.

steps.title: Turn amounts into numbers
steps.text: Exercise 2: parse_amount.

steps.title: Clean each row
steps.text: Exercise 3: clean_row.

steps.title: Remove duplicate customers
steps.text: Exercise 4: remove_duplicates.

steps.title: Find the late customers
steps.text: Exercise 5: late_customers.

steps.title: Make the report
steps.text: Exercise 6: make_report.

steps.title: Add tests with assert
steps.text: Test normal, edge and bad cases.

steps.title: Handle bad input kindly
steps.text: Keep the good rows and report the bad ones.

steps.title: Write the README
steps.text: One sentence, the problem, how to run it, example output.

steps.title: Put it on GitHub
steps.text: Add a .gitignore first, so no private files are saved.

steps.title: Write a post about it
steps.text: Use the hook, problem, steps, result, lesson.

projects.title: Customer message sorter
projects.summary: Sort fake customer messages into labels with a fake AI model, then swap in a real one on your PC.

steps.title: Plan it on one page
steps.text: Say what goes in, what comes out, and when it is done.

steps.title: Build the prompt
steps.text: Exercise 1: build_classify_prompt.

steps.title: Ask the model and check the answer
steps.text: Exercise 2: classify.

steps.title: Try again when the answer is bad
steps.text: Exercise 3: classify_with_retry.

steps.title: Sort all the messages
steps.text: Exercise 4: sort_messages.

steps.title: Make the report
steps.text: Exercise 5: make_report.

steps.title: Test it with a fake model
steps.text: Fake models make tests steady and free.

steps.title: Try a real model on your PC
steps.text: Use an environment variable for the key. Fake messages only.

steps.title: Write the README
steps.text: Explain what it does and how to run it.

steps.title: Put it on GitHub

steps.title: Write a post about it
steps.text: Be honest about what you did and learned.
